land.text: Kedah, where 'King Phra Ong Mahawangsa converted to Islam and adopted the name Sultan Mudzafar Shah'

successors.note: The Kedah Sultanate page dates the conversion to 1136 (infobox) and calls the date 'unlikely'; an Acehnese account says 1474. The sultanate-of-kedah dossier starts 1136 with Srivijaya as counterpart.

capitals.name: Bujang Valley (Sungai Batu, Merbok River)
capitals.note: The Kedah Sultanate page says 'In 634 CE, a new kingdom was formed in Kedah, with its capital at Langkasuka' (a Kedah-Langkasuka identification no other page makes); Sungai Batu on the Merbok River is the researcher's pin for the Bujang Valley settlement. The sultanate's Bukit Meriam seat (1136) is in the sultanate-of-kedah dossier.

correction.text: Kedah: the Bujang Valley between Mount Jerai and the Muda River, 'dominated the northern plains of the Malay Peninsula'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). The Bujang Valley complex is 'a sprawling 5th to 14th century CE Indianised Hindu-Buddhist historical complex' of 224 km2 enlarged to 1,000 km2 by Sungai Batu, 'between 1,217-metre Mount Jerai in the north and Muda River in the south'; 'a clay brick monument dating back to 110 AD'. The drawn shape is the whole of Kedah state (about 9,500 km2), a coarse over-cover of that infobox-sized settlement; the Kedah page's 'dominated the northern plains' is its only extent. Infobox area: none.

correction.text: Kedah: the Bujang Valley between Mount Jerai and the Muda River, 'dominated the northern plains of the Malay Peninsula'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Kedah fell outside the influence of Sanfoqi during the 11th century' (Srivijaya page), and the Cholas 'captured the King of Kadaram' in 1025 and 'Virarajendra Chola ... conquered Kadaram (Kedah) and gave it back to its king': Kedah is again a kingdom of its own. The srivijaya dossier keeps Kedah in Srivijaya until 1139 (Cliopatria's year) and the sultanate-of-kedah dossier takes it from Srivijaya in 1136: the three dossiers disagree about 1026-1135 and the reviewer should reconcile them.

region.text: Kedah: the Bujang Valley between Mount Jerai and the Muda River, 'dominated the northern plains of the Malay Peninsula'

ledger.note: c. 330: Old Kedah begins. The Kedah Sultanate page labels the predecessor state 'Old Kedah (330-1136)' and lists a first Durbar Raja at 330-390 with dates it calls speculative; the Bujang Valley page has a brick monument 'dating back to 110 AD' and Hindus arriving 'around 170 CE'. The founding year is a page label, not a dated event.

634: a new kingdom is formed in Kedah. 'In 634 CE, a new kingdom was formed in Kedah' after Maharaja Derbar Raja of Gombroon was shipwrecked 'in around 630 CE' (legend of the Kedah Annals); same state, same colour (rule 2).

region.text: Kedah: the Bujang Valley between Mount Jerai and the Muda River, 'dominated the northern plains of the Malay Peninsula'

ledger.note: c. 682-685: Srivijaya conquers Kedah. Srivijaya infobox 'Conquest of Kedah: c. 682-685'; Kalah/Kedah is among Srivijaya's main urban centres 'Muara Jambi and Kedah'. The srivijaya dossier carries the matching gain at 685.

region.text: Kedah: the Bujang Valley between Mount Jerai and the Muda River, 'dominated the northern plains of the Malay Peninsula'

ledger.note: 1026: Kedah is again its own kingdom. 'Kedah fell outside the influence of Sanfoqi during the 11th century' (Srivijaya page) and 'Between 1017 and 1025, the Chola Empire raided the main Malay ports ... including Kedah' and 'captured the King of Kadaram'; the page gives the century, not the year, so 1026 (after the raid) is the researcher's bridging judgment, a gap.

region.text: Kedah: the Bujang Valley between Mount Jerai and the Muda River, 'dominated the northern plains of the Malay Peninsula'

ledger.note: 1136: the king of Kedah becomes a Muslim sultan. 'At-Tarikh Salasilah Negeri Kedah described the conversion to Islam as starting in 1136 AD'; 'King Phra Ong Mahawangsa converted to Islam and adopted the name Sultan Mudzafar Shah'. The page calls 1136 'unlikely' (an Acehnese account says 1474) and says Kedah 'may have remained Hindu-Buddhist until the 15th century'; the Kadaram of the Cholas was destroyed by Kulottunga in c. 1120 (Srivijaya page).

wars.name: Chola raids on Kadaram (Kedah)
wars.outcome: 'Between 1017 and 1025, the Chola Empire raided the main Malay ports ... including Kedah' and captured its king; Virarajendra 'conquered Kadaram (Kedah) and gave it back to its king'; 'Kulottunga stayed in Kadaram (Kedah) after the naval expedition of 1067'; the Tamil poem Kalingatupparani of c. 1120 mentions 'Kulottungga's destruction of Kadaram'.
wars.note: Raids and sackings, no annexation: the Chola dossier would carry any occupation. A Chola inscription of 1086 found in Kedah is on the Kedah Tua page (not a territorial event).

wars.name: Srivijaya's conquest of Kedah

zones.text: Kedah: the Bujang Valley between Mount Jerai and the Muda River, 'dominated the northern plains of the Malay Peninsula'

wars.outcome: 'Conquest of Kedah: c. 682-685'; Kedah becomes one of Srivijaya's main urban centres.
wars.note: The campaign is a single infobox line; the Kedah Tua page has only 'After the 7th century, Srivijaya took Kedah as a vassal'.

certainty.note: The page gives the Bujang Valley's size but no frontier; the whole of Kedah state is a coarse stand-in.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for Old Kedah (its Sultanate of Kedah row starts 1139). Wikidata id not looked up (wikidata.org unreachable): null. The 'Kedah Tua' page is a general history of Kedah without an infobox; the dates 330-1136 come from the Kedah Sultanate page's status label. 685-1025: the land belongs to Srivijaya in the srivijaya dossier (gain 685, loss 1139), so this dossier draws nothing; 1026-1135 is the researcher's bridging reading from the Srivijaya page (Kedah outside Sanfoqi's influence in the 11th century, the king of Kadaram captured in 1025 and restored) and conflicts with the srivijaya and sultanate-of-kedah dossiers, which both hold Kedah under Srivijaya to 1136/1139. The Kedah Sultanate page itself says Srivijaya was 'in direct control' at the (disputed) 1136 conversion. A gap-filler should read the Chola Empire page. Whether Kedah Tua and Langkasuka are one polity is not settled: the Kedah Sultanate page puts the 634 kingdom's capital at Langkasuka.
